sections.content: To describe how a city changes, Spanish combines past, present and time expressions. The imperfect describes earlier situations, while the indefinido can mark a specific change or turning point. Expressions such as antes, con el tiempo, desde entonces and cada vez más help organise development over time.

items.spanish: Antes había menos tráfico, pero la ciudad ha crecido mucho.
items.english: There used to be less traffic, but the city has grown a lot.

items.spanish: El barrio era más tranquilo antes de que construyeran la nueva avenida.
items.english: The neighbourhood was quieter before they built the new avenue.

items.spanish: Con el tiempo, la zona se transformó y aparecieron nuevos comercios.
items.english: Over time, the area was transformed and new shops appeared.

items.spanish: Desde entonces, el tráfico ha aumentado y las calles están más llenas.
items.english: Since then, traffic has increased and the streets are busier.

sections.content: Use time expressions to show the relationship between stages of change. The imperfect gives background, while a completed event can mark a turning point.
